nodes.Name: FS
nodes.DocComment:
An FS provides access to a hierarchical file system.

The FS interface is the minimum implementation required of the file system.
A file system may implement additional interfaces,
such as [ReadFileFS], to provide additional or optimized functionality.

[testing/fstest.TestFS] may be used to test implementations of an FS for
correctness.

nodes.Name: ValidPath
nodes.DocComment:
ValidPath reports whether the given path name
is valid for use in a call to Open.

Note that paths are slash-separated on all systems, even Windows.
Paths containing other characters such as backslash and colon
are accepted as valid, but those characters must never be
interpreted by an [FS] implementation as path element separators.
See the [Path Names] section for more details.

[Path Names]: https://pkg.go.dev/io/fs#hdr-Path_Names

nodes.Name: File
nodes.DocComment:
A File provides access to a single file.
The File interface is the minimum implementation required of the file.
Directory files should also implement [ReadDirFile].
A file may implement [io.ReaderAt] or [io.Seeker] as optimizations.

nodes.Name: DirEntry
nodes.DocComment:
A DirEntry is an entry read from a directory
(using the [ReadDir] function or a [ReadDirFile]'s ReadDir method).

nodes.Name: ReadDirFile
nodes.DocComment:
A ReadDirFile is a directory file whose entries can be read with the ReadDir method.
Every directory file should implement this interface.
(It is permissible for any file to implement this interface,
but if so ReadDir should return an error for non-directories.)

nodes.DocComment:

nodes.Name: FileInfo
nodes.DocComment: A FileInfo describes a file and is returned by [Stat].

nodes.Name: FileMode
nodes.DocComment:
A FileMode represents a file's mode and permission bits.
The bits have the same definition on all systems, so that
information about files can be moved from one system
to another portably. Not all bits apply to all systems.
The only required bit is [ModeDir] for directories.

nodes.Name: ModeDir
nodes.DocComment:
The defined file mode bits are the most significant bits of the [FileMode].
The nine least-significant bits are the standard Unix rwxrwxrwx permissions.
The values of these bits should be considered part of the public API and
may be used in wire protocols or disk representations: they must not be
changed, although new bits might be added.

nodes.Name: IsDir
nodes.DocComment:
IsDir reports whether m describes a directory.
That is, it tests for the [ModeDir] bit being set in m.

nodes.Name: IsRegular
nodes.DocComment:
IsRegular reports whether m describes a regular file.
That is, it tests that no mode type bits are set.

nodes.Name: Perm
nodes.DocComment: Perm returns the Unix permission bits in m (m & [ModePerm]).

nodes.Name: Type
nodes.DocComment: Type returns type bits in m (m & [ModeType]).

nodes.Name: PathError
nodes.DocComment: PathError records an error and the operation and file path that caused it.

nodes.Name: Timeout
nodes.DocComment: Timeout reports whether this error represents a timeout.
